## Team Project Presentation Goals

- **Poster Deadlines & Specs:** What needs to be submitted, when, and how it should be formatted
- **Design Principles:** Making your research clear, readable, and visually compelling
- **Session Format:** How the rotating poster session works
- **Presentation Best Practices:** How to deliver a sharp 6-minute pitch

- **Poster PDF Due:** Thursday, **December 10 at 11:59 PM** via ELMS
  - *Strict deadline:* Late submissions may not be printed in time
  - Instructors handle printing
  - Poster will be waiting for you at your table on presentation day

  - Arrive promptly, we will precisely follow the schedule

## Physical Specs & Originality

- **Dimensions:** **29" × 39"** (Portrait orientation)
  - Approximately your team table monitor, rotated 90 degrees
- **100% Original Analysis:**
  - Summarize your team's original question, data analysis, and main results
  - **No outside charts or tables** (unlike the fact sheets, cited third-party plots are not allowed here)
- **Images:** Must be original, public domain, or properly licensed (Creative Commons) with required attribution included on the poster

---

## Visual Design: Less Is More

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
### [Do]{.underline}
- Treat the poster as a **visual anchor** for a conversation, not a printed paper
- Lead with your **best original visualizations**
- Leave plenty of **whitespace** so the eye can breathe
- Use a **light background** with dark, high-contrast text
:::

::: {.column width="10%"}

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
### [Don't]{.underline}
- Write dense walls of text or paste paragraphs
- Use large, solid-color backgrounds—especially **dark backgrounds with white/light text**
- Mix too many different fonts, sizes, or competing colors
:::
:::

---

## Typography & Readability (4–6 Feet Rule)

Everything (except perhaps references) must be readable while standing approximately 4-6 feet from 
the poster:

| Poster Element | Recommended Size | Style |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Title** | 85–90 pt | Sans Serif |
| **Authors** | 56–60 pt | Sans Serif |
| **Sub-headings** | 36–48 pt | Sans Serif |
| **Body Text** | 22–24 pt | Serif |
| **Captions / References** | 16–18 pt | Serif |

## Font Styles

**Serif** $\text{fonts have decorative serifs in the letters}$

- e.g., Times New Roman, Georgia, Cambria

**Sans Serif** fonts do not have decorative serifs

- e.g., Arial, Calibri, Helvetica, Book Antiqua

## Session Format & Timing {.smaller}

The session runs from **4:00 PM – 6:00 PM** in 2309 ESJ on a rigid schedule:

- **4:00 PM – 4:10 PM (10 min):** Arrive, pick up your printed poster, and hang it at your assigned station
- **4:10 PM – 5:30 PM:** **10 simultaneous presentation stations** rotating every **12 minutes**
  - **6 minutes:** Live presentation 
  - **2 minutes:** Brief Q&A
  - **2 minutes:** Complete peer evaluation
  - **2 minutes:** Transition to the next station
- **Six** total sessions
- Each student provided with an individualized schedule
  - **Present Once**: Designates one session in which they present their poster
  - **Observe 5**: Designates a different poster presentation to observe and peer evaluate each session
- **5:30:** Submit peer evaluations and clean up

## Session Technical Details {.smaller}

- You will receive a printed, personalized schedule/peer evaluation sheet at the start
- Session assignments will be **assigned randomly** so that
  - Each student presents exactly once than once
  - No more than one person from each team presents in each session

  - No student evaluates the same team more than once
- Time kept with an automated system 
  - Display of time remaining on projection screens
  - Audio signals to move on to the next step
- Students are required to participate in every session

## Your Dual Role: Presenter & Evaluator

- **When Presenting:**
  - You will be assigned a specific time slot(s) to staff your team's poster and present
  - Keep an eye on the clock, rotations are strict so everyone gets their full time
- **When Not Presenting:**
  - You will receive a personalized schedule of posters to visit
  - You are responsible for **watching and completing peer evaluations** for your assigned presentations
  - Bring a pen and move promptly during the 2-minute transitions

## How to Structure a Great 6-Minute Pitch

Don't read your poster word-for-word. Tell a clear, 6-minute story:

1. **The Hook & Question (0:45):** What problem are you solving, and why should anyone care?
2. **Data & Approach (1:15):** Briefly explain what data you used and how you analyzed it (skip tedious minutiae unless asked)
3. **Key Findings & Visuals (2:30):** Walk your audience directly through your main charts—point to specific patterns and explain what they mean
4. **Takeaway (1:00):** State your core conclusion clearly and leave the listeners with your main conclusions in their head


---

## Poster Presentation Best Practices

- **Face your audience, not the poster:** Stand to the side of the board and use open body language so the whole semi-circle can see and hear you
- **Use the visuals actively:** Point to axes, trends, and callouts on your plots as you speak—make the poster work for you
- **Practice with a timer:** 6 minutes goes faster than you think; rehearse until you can hit your main takeaway comfortably in ~5:30
- **Know your limitations:** If someone asks a tough methodological question, answer honestly—acknowledging caveats shows rigor
